note: Borderline relevance cases from the hand-checked batches, grouped into types for a policy decision. Members are 'batch:ordinal'; batch 10-02 = runs/2026-10-02, 10-03 and 10-04 likewise. 'anchors' are confidently-judged examples included to make a type concrete.

types.title: Builds AI agents or LLM systems for internal teams
types.description: Engineers whose work is building AI systems (agents, LLM platforms, fine-tuning, evaluation, AIOps) whose users are other engineers or internal operations, not external customers. Prompt 1.3.0 made Sol reject these as 'AI-assisted engineering'.
types.why: Building an agent or an LLM platform is AI engineering whoever the users are. Only using AI tools (Copilot, Claude) is not.

types.title: Uses AI tools, or AI is only hedged or listed
types.description: Ordinary engineering roles where AI appears as tools the engineer uses (coding assistants, AI-driven EDA flows), as a hedge ('potentially leveraging AI', 'identify opportunities to integrate LLMs'), or as one item in a long skills list.
types.why: Nothing in the work is building or operating AI. Showing these would flood the report: most postings now mention AI tools.

types.title: Ordinary engineering role that requires AI-building skills
types.description: Generic duties (web, backend, C++), but the REQUIRED qualifications ask for hands-on experience building with LLMs, RAG, GenAI applications or ML models.
types.why: A hard requirement to build with AI usually means the team does it, even when the duty list is boilerplate. Mere 'knowledge of' is weaker.

types.title: Google's standard 'integrating GenAI tools into workflows' requirement
types.description: Google engineering-manager and staff postings that add one minimum qualification: 'Experience integrating generative AI tools or LLM interfaces into workflows'. The rest of the posting is a normal SWE role.
types.why: The line appears on many unrelated Google postings, so it is closer to template text, but it is a hard requirement.

types.title: Customer-facing engineers for AI products
types.description: Customer engineers, solution/readiness architects, support and success engineers whose product is AI (Agentforce, an AI security product, an industrial AI monitoring product, Cloud AI).
types.why: The prompt already treats these as peripheral: AI is the main subject even though they do not build the models.

types.title: Consultants and enterprise architects who advise on AI among other things
types.description: Billable consulting managers, enterprise architects and practice leads whose engagements include designing or integrating AI solutions for clients, alongside CRM, cloud or data work.
types.why: Judged both ways so far. They do design AI solutions, but the job is consulting delivery, and most are very senior.

types.title: Product, program and strategy roles where AI is the main subject
types.description: Product managers, product owners and strategy leads who define AI features or AI automation but do not engineer them.
types.why: AI is central, but the work is not engineering. Depends on whether you would apply to an AI product-management role.

types.title: Data engineering, BI and architecture whose output feeds ML
types.description: Data engineers, BI engineers and data architects whose pipelines or platforms are consumed by data scientists or AI features, among other users.
types.why: Data platforms serve everyone; ML is one consumer. Show only when the role builds ML-specific infrastructure (feature stores, training data, model serving).

types.title: ML appears only in a company or job-family template
types.description: Barclays' standard 'Collaboration with data scientist to build and deploy machine learning models' block, Google's 'AI and Infrastructure' org paragraph, and similar boilerplate. The role-specific part is ETL, migration or general software.
types.why: The same sentence appears on Pega, SRE and C++ postings, so it says nothing about this job.

types.title: 'Data Scientist' or quant titles doing analytics and statistics
types.description: Roles titled Data Scientist (or similar) whose duties are business analytics, experimentation, forecasting, pricing or credit strategy, sometimes with propensity or churn models.
types.why: The title names data science and many build predictive models. Hiding them would miss roles a data-science candidate would apply to.

types.title: Chip and hardware work for AI accelerators
types.description: Design verification, SoC and interconnect roles where AI/ML accelerators or AI cluster interconnect (UALink) are among the things designed or verified.
types.why: The prompt calls hardware for AI accelerators peripheral. Weaker when AI is one item in a long list of blocks.

types.title: Model risk, AI governance, AI quality and AI security
types.description: Model validation, AI governance or privacy, quality leads who measure AI model accuracy, benchmarking of AI outputs, and identity/security controls for AI agents.
types.why: AI is the object of the work, but nobody builds models. Closer to oversight than engineering.

types.title: Data labelling and annotation roles
types.description: Amazon 'ML Data Associate' style postings: non-technical labelling of text, image and video data for model training. Usually early-career.
types.why: Both models currently show them. They are ML jobs in name and early-career, but explicitly non-technical.

types.title: Systems next to AI, without building it
types.description: ADAS algorithm integration and simulation, software that talks to computer-vision or robotics systems, OCR as one feature, notification platforms for agents, QA of ML-assisted decisions, serving infrastructure for AI features.
types.why: The role touches AI outputs but the duties never say they build, train or evaluate models.
